summary: Clarify token-accounting for scheduled workers versus webhook retry loops causing intermittent 429s
description: Customer BrightData Labs reports intermittent 429 throttles during their hourly embedding backfill job. They run a scheduled worker that fires parallel curl-based upload tasks and also have webhook retry logic that retries failed webhooks aggressively. Customer is confused how tokens are being attributed between scheduled/background workers and short-lived webhook retry attempts, and is seeing tenant-level 429s even though individual route headers show remaining credits. They request guidance on how to isolate background vs interactive traffic and whether they should configure separate routes/priority classes or rely on smoothing and burst pools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run scheduled worker that concurrently posts 100 small embedding requests (approx 128 tokens each) using the same API key, parallelism 20.
2) Meanwhile trigger webhook endpoints from external service; webhook handler retries with exponential backoff but initial retries happen within 10-30s window.
3) Observe 429 responses across embedding endpoints and some chat endpoints for ~2-4 minutes during the hourly run.
4) Capture response headers from API (x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset, x-retry-after) and compare tenant console quota charts.
5) Confirm tenant-level quota graph shows token depletion spike overlapping with scheduled worker window and webhook retry bursts.
Curl example to simulate worker load:
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"input":"test $i"}' & done
logs: [2026-03-01T14:02:08Z] route=/v1/embeddings tenant_id=bdl123 tokens=128 - accepted: false - reason=tenant_quota_exhausted
[2026-03-01T14:02:09Z] webhook_retry attempt=3 status=504 -> retry queued, subsequent attempt triggered within 20s
[2026-03-01T14:05:32Z] tenant_quota_refill observed - refill_delta: +20000 tokens, normal operation resumes
investigation: Support replicated a scaled-down version using the customer's parallelism pattern; saw tenant-level 429s once concurrent in-flight token usage crossed burst window threshold.
Console metrics and per-route headers indicated route-level remaining credits while tenant bucket was depleted, indicating aggregated tenant accounting (background + webhook) caused exhaustion.

Hypothesis: webhook retries, which are short-lived and bursty, combined with scheduled worker fanout, consume burst credits that are not isolated by default. The customer's current setup uses a single route and API key for both worker and webhook traffic.

Checked rate-limiter config for the tenant: smoothing_enabled=true, burst_window=60s, burst_capacity=25000 tokens. Observed hourly spike exceeded burst_capacity before smoothing reduced rate, causing transient 429s.
Reviewed tenant refill schedule and discovered refill ticks align to minute boundaries; heavy concurrency concentrated in same minute causes sawtooth depletion.

Suggested immediate mitigation: throttle worker concurrency (reduce parallelism) or add jitter to webhook retries; longer-term: configure separate route for background jobs or request isolated burst pool.
Support requested temporary logs and a small set of request IDs to correlate with origin; customer provided three request IDs in comments.
comments: Customer (Aaron, BrightData): We're seeing 10-15% of embedding calls return 429 during the hourly job. Console shows route-level remaining tokens — why is tenant exhausted?

Support (Maya): Thanks Aaron — the most likely reason is tenant-level aggregation across routes. Can you share a couple of request IDs from the 429s? Also, confirm whether webhook retries and scheduled workers use the same API key.
Customer (Aaron): We use a single org key for both. IDs: req_20260301_14_02_07a, req_20260301_14_02_08b, req_20260301_14_02_09c. Worker parallelism is 20, each request ~128 tokens.

SRE (Ethan): We've correlated req_...07a to a background worker fanout. Tenant bucket was at 0 at that minute. Route header showed remaining because per-route bucket had different smoothing and hadn't hit its local route hard-limit yet. Tenant-level enforcement is authoritative.

Support (Maya): Temporary workaround: reduce worker parallelism to 8-10 or stagger the batch over 2-3 minutes. We can also create an isolated route for background jobs; that requires console change or a support action to add a route-level quota. Would you like us to provision a separate route for testing?
Customer (Aaron): Please provision a separate route for background jobs to test isolation. Also would appreciate documentation that explains how tenant vs route buckets interact.

SRE (Ethan): Provisioned test route 'bdl-background' and applied burst pool isolation & a lower priority class for background jobs on 2026-03-02. Please update your worker to use the new route key (we provided a short-lived test key).
resolution: Provisioned separate route 'bdl-background' with an isolated burst pool and a dedicated API key for scheduled workers. Customer updated their worker to use the new key and reduced initial parallelism during the rollout window. Observed no tenant-level 429s during the next hourly run. Follow-up actions: create a KB article detailing best practices for separating background/batch traffic versus interactive/webhook traffic; recommend default rate-limiter tiering and sample configs. Customer confirmed acceptance on 2026-03-03.
